title: Operational Administrator

description:

title: Payroll Specialist
description:
Payroll & Finance Administrator

Salary: £38,379 per annum
Location: Lincoln - 100% onsite
Contract: Permanent, full-time (37 hours per week)
Closing Date: ASAP / Ongoing - applications considered on a rolling basis

Marble Mayne Recruitment is delighted to be supporting a Students' Union in Lincoln with the recruitment of a Payroll & Finance Administrator. This is a newly created position offering an exciting opportunity for an experienced payroll professional to take ownership of a significant payroll improvement project, whilst also supporting the wider finance function.

The organisation employs approximately 70 permanent staff alongside a further 60 student and bar staff, creating a varied and relatively complex payroll environment.

Currently, payroll administration involves a combination of spreadsheets, timesheet systems and manual processes, with the University undertaking the final tax calculations. The organisation is now looking to bring its payroll operations fully in-house, with the ambition of developing a streamlined, automated, one-stop payroll solution by early to mid-2028.

This is a fantastic opportunity for someone who enjoys getting under the skin of existing processes, identifying improvements and implementing more efficient ways of working.

About the Role

Reporting to the Group Finance Manager, the role will be approximately 70% payroll focused and 30% broader finance administration.

Initially, you will need to develop a thorough understanding of how payroll currently operates across the organisation, taking ownership of existing processes whilst reviewing opportunities to improve accuracy, efficiency and automation.

Working closely with senior finance and HR colleagues, you will play a central role in designing and implementing a new integrated payroll solution, reducing manual intervention and ultimately bringing the entire payroll process together.

Alongside this project, you will be responsible for ensuring accurate and timely payroll administration, including timesheet management, payroll calculations, statutory deductions, pensions, reconciliations and compliance with relevant legislation.

The remaining 30% of the role will involve supporting the wider finance team with purchase and sales ledger processing, expenses, reconciliations, month-end activities and general financial administration.

About You

We are looking for someone with strong, hands-on, end-to-end payroll experience who is comfortable working in a varied and potentially complex payroll environment.

Ideally, you will have worked within a small/medium sized organisation where you have needed to take responsibility for multiple aspects of payroll, rather than specialising in one narrow area within a large payroll department.

Experience within hospitality, commercial organisations, charities or similarly varied environments would be particularly relevant.

You will need to demonstrate experience of managing payroll for a mixture of permanent salaried employees and weekly paid, casual or variable-hours staff, including dealing with different pay rates, timesheets and working patterns.

Strong knowledge of UK payroll legislation, statutory deductions, pensions and payroll systems is essential, alongside excellent Excel skills.

Importantly, we are also looking for someone who enjoys improving processes and systems. Previous experience of implementing payroll improvements, introducing automation or supporting a payroll systems transition would be particularly valuable.

As this is a combined payroll and finance position, you will also need some practical finance or accounting experience, ideally including transaction processing, reconciliations and working with accounting systems.

You will be organised, accurate, proactive and confident working independently, with the communication skills to engage effectively with colleagues across the organisation.

Location and Working Arrangements

Please note that this is a 100% onsite position based in Lincoln, with no hybrid or remote working arrangements available. Due to the operational nature of the role, the need to work closely with colleagues and the significant payroll transformation project ahead, the successful candidate will be required to work onsite five days per week.

Application Process

Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis, with no fixed closing date. Early applications are therefore encouraged.

title: Activities Coordinator

description:

About the Role

Avon Search is currently recruiting for a passionate and enthusiastic Activities Co-ordinator to join a welcoming and established 46-bedded care home in Gainsborough.

This is an excellent opportunity for someone who enjoys working with older people and has a genuine passion for creating meaningful, engaging and enjoyable activities that enhance residents' quality of life.

Working closely with the care team, you will be responsible for planning, organising and delivering a varied programme of activities tailored to residents' individual interests, abilities and needs.

The home supports older people living with dementia and provides residential, dementia, respite and day care. You will play an important role in promoting social interaction, maintaining independence and encouraging residents to remain active, involved and connected.

The successful candidate will be friendly, creative, organised and confident engaging with residents, relatives and colleagues.

This is a 36-hour-per-week position, offering a rewarding opportunity within a supportive care environment.

About the Home

The home is a welcoming 46-bedded care home in Gainsborough, providing residential, dementia, respite and day care for older people.

Supported by a skilled and friendly team of carers, the home is committed to delivering high standards of person-centred care, ensuring residents feel comfortable, supported and valued.

The home's care philosophy places great importance on promoting dignity, independence and individual choice, while ensuring residents' health, safety and security.

Residents are encouraged to maintain an active lifestyle and continue enjoying their personal interests, with care and support tailored to their individual needs.

Key features include:
- Established 46-bedded care home.
- Residential, dementia, respite and day care services.
- Skilled, friendly and supportive care team.
- Strong focus on dignity, independence and individual choice.
- Encouragement of residents' hobbies, interests and active lifestyles.

Key Responsibilities
- Plan, organise and deliver a varied programme of activities for residents.
- Arrange group and individual activities based on residents' interests and abilities.
- Encourage participation and social interaction.
- Organise creative activities, games, music, entertainment and reminiscence sessions.
- Support residents living with dementia to participate in meaningful activities.
- Promote independence, confidence and emotional wellbeing.
- Build positive relationships with residents, relatives and colleagues.
- Encourage residents to maintain existing hobbies and discover new interests.
- Work alongside the care team to ensure activities are inclusive and accessible.
- Maintain records of activities and resident participation.
- Adapt activities to suit individual needs and abilities.

Candidate Requirements

Essential:
- Previous experience working with older people, ideally within a care home or similar setting.
- A genuine passion for organising activities and engaging with residents.
- Friendly, caring and approachable personality.
- Creative, enthusiastic and confident in delivering activities.
- Excellent communication and interpersonal skills.
- Good organisational and time-management abilities.
- Ability to work independently and as part of a team.
- Understanding of the importance of dignity, respect and person-centred care.
- Flexible and adaptable approach to residents' individual needs.

Benefits & Perks
- £14.00 per hour.

title: Team Administrator

The Clinical Decisions Unit provides an environment and atmosphere that is conducive to enabling service users to access high-quality, thorough assessments leading to well-developed service user centred treatment plans. This will enable the service user to both manage their immediate crisis and support them into a (usually community-based) pathway, leading to more robust recovery. Distribute information within the Primary Mental Health Care Teams as necessary. title: GP Receptionist / Care Navigator
description: Tasburgh Lodge Surgery is located in the beautiful village of Woodhall Spa. An opportunity has arisen to recruit an enthusiastic, motivated and forward-thinking Receptionist / Care Navigator to work part-time or full time (up to 30 hrs p/w) within our dedicated reception team. We are looking for a team player wanting to help our surgery continue with its great success and contribute to its key performance measures and development. Experience in general practice as well as familiarity with SystmOne would be a distinct advantage but is not essential. Main dutues of the role: Greeting and welcoming patients and visitors - Making a good 'first impression', dealing with enquiries at the front desk and handing out prescriptions. Answering and direting phone calls handling enquiries, taking messages, and transferring calls to the right person. Managing appointments - booking, rescheduling and confirming appointments. Handling incoming and outgoing mail - sorting post and generic emails. Maintaining the reception area - keeping it tidy, stocked with supplies, and professional-looking. Managing records and data entry - updating contact details, logging visitor information, and maintaining accurate records. Providing administrative support - helping wih filing, photocopying, scanning or basic correspondence. Dealing with general enquiries - in person, by phone or via email. Assisting staff or management - supporting internal communication, registrations, chaperoning and opening and closing of practice premises as and when required. Job summary Medical Receptionist / Care Navigator We are seeking a friendly, professional, and highly organised Medical Receptionist/Care Navigator to join our busy GP practice. As the first point of contact for patients, you will provide excellent customer service both face-to-face and over the telephone, ensuring patients are directed to the most appropriate healthcare professional or service. Key responsibilities include managing appointments, handling patient enquiries, processing registrations, maintaining accurate patient records, supporting administrative functions, and working closely with clinicians and practice staff to ensure the smooth running of the surgery. You will also assess and prioritise requests, including home visit requests, while maintaining strict patient confidentiality at all times. The successful candidate will have excellent communication and IT skills, a professional and compassionate manner, strong organisational abilities, and the confidence to work independently in a fast-paced environment. Previous reception, customer service, or healthcare experience is desirable but not essential, as full training will be provided. This is an excellent opportunity to contribute to high-quality patient care within a supportive and dedicated primary care team.
